event.active_recruitment_new_cast_01_aft: You front one thousand Berrys for another sale day. {{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}} stays at the market to run it.
You leave the choice open. {{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}} packs the tiles without calling another number.
{{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}} snaps the last chalk stick in two, leaves half at the market, and accepts a berth aboard.
{{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}} closes the cashbox after the final hammer. The market owner offers more money to stay, but she stares at the broken chalk in her fingers instead of the contract.
event.active_recruitment_new_cast_01_auc: You spend five hundred Berrys on tarps and line. {{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}} saves the numbers before they wash away.
You overheat the room; two buyers start fighting and the auction stops.
The crowd chants every number back. {{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}} finishes the auction to an absurd ovation.
Half the buyers leave before the rain eases.
You turn the wait into a bidding game. {{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}} keeps enough buyers to finish.
You mix the deposits and sell a lot already paid for; merchants demand their money back.
You even find two hidden commissions. {{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}} calls them out before the final lot.
The chalk marks wash away too quickly to recover the full order.
You rebuild the order from the dry receipts. {{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}} can finish without shorting a seller.
A downpour turns {{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}}’s lot numbers into white streaks. Sellers want paying before they leave, buyers demand their lots, and the main ledger is already soaked.
event.active_recruitment_new_cast_01_bla: You commission one last notice. {{npc_active_recruit_notice_carver}} stays on the road with one more job.
You leave the board blank. {{npc_active_recruit_notice_carver}} keeps it as the first job not yet decided.
{{npc_active_recruit_notice_carver}} flips the last board, cuts a small mark into the back, and accepts a berth aboard.
{{npc_active_recruit_notice_carver}} has packed every plate except one blank board. The guard returned her tools, but every town now orders notices before she even chooses where to go.
event.active_recruitment_new_cast_01_bra: {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} gives you a blank tag: “For someone who comes back.”
{{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} keeps the bell and heads for the next port where someone is waiting for news.
{{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} packs away the bell, keeps only a handful of blank tags, and accepts a berth aboard.
{{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} sets a blank tag in front of you. After two deaths were declared too quickly, he refuses to carve another name until he chooses what to do for the living.
event.active_recruitment_new_cast_01_cha: You shout a bid high enough to freeze the room. {{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}} gets a few seconds to recount the tiles.
Bid on 47
You miss the tile and topple two stalls; the thief vanishes in the crush.
You catch the tile and the bag of stolen numbers. {{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}} takes control of the whole auction again.
The tile changes hands again before you can grab it.
You recover number 47 at the roof edge. {{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}} can stop the sale before the wrong lot.
Catch the tile
You accuse the wrong buyer and start a fight between two merchant families.
You also see where the thief hid the other numbers. {{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}} saves the entire auction.
The tiles move too fast to see who switched the number.
You spot the chalk-stained sleeve. {{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}} knows exactly whom to chase.
Spot the switch
In the middle of a dock auction, tile 47 vanishes between bids. {{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}}, running the chalk lots, jumps onto a table: the next hammer would sell the wrong cargo.
Number 47
You block the only ladder. {{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}} recovers the bag of tiles before the thief can rejoin the crowd.
Block the ladder
You restart the bidding from the street. The crowd keeps watching you while {{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}} climbs.
Call the bid
The thief drops the bag to run faster. {{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}} gets the numbers back, not the culprit.
Wait for the drop
The thief climbs above the market with the bag of tiles. {{npc_active_recruit_lot_runner}} stays below to stop the hammer, but the crowd is already demanding the next lot.
Along the Roofline
event.active_recruitment_new_cast_01_fac: The clerk paints you as an accomplice and calls for guards.
The clerk even provides a fresh board. {{npc_active_recruit_notice_carver}} finally gets a clean surface.
He resumes pasting over the wall as soon as you stop talking.
The clerk grants ten minutes. {{npc_active_recruit_notice_carver}} already has the carving tools open.
Hold back the clerk
You let the clerk finish. {{npc_active_recruit_notice_carver}} copies from memory whatever remains visible.
Leave the wall
You tear away the original notice too; the crowd thinks you are destroying evidence.
You also recover a date and quay name. {{npc_active_recruit_notice_carver}} can remake the notice without losing the trail.
The paste has eaten the ink and no face comes through clearly.
Under three posters, you recover the missing portrait. {{npc_active_recruit_notice_carver}} immediately carves the rescued details.
Peel the layers
A clerk is pasting tax notices over a missing-person poster. {{npc_active_recruit_notice_carver}}, an itinerant carver, drives a gouge into the wall and demands ten minutes to save the face.
The Face Under the Paste
{{npc_active_recruit_notice_carver}} carves the recovered quay mark into the corner of the board. It becomes the only usable lead.
Copy the quay mark
You leave the wall. {{npc_active_recruit_notice_carver}} keeps the board and follows the lead alone.
Leave the clue
You help print two copies before the clerk changes his mind.
Make two copies
The wet paper finally comes free. Beneath the portrait, {{npc_active_recruit_notice_carver}} finds a tiny quay mark the new notice would have covered completely.
Under the Paste
event.active_recruitment_new_cast_01_las: You declare the account settled. {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} unties your knot with a surprised smile.
{{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} stays on the docks and promises to settle your favor the next time paths cross.
{{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} cuts off the last client knot, keeps the one linking you, and accepts a berth aboard.
{{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} waits at the end of the quay with an almost empty cord. The creditors are settled; only one knot bears your name, and no client still ties this life down.
event.active_recruitment_new_cast_01_mir: The disputed sheet leaves the sale. {{npc_active_recruit_notice_carver}} keeps the tools and the bad proof as evidence.
The guard compares the matrices and releases the tools. {{npc_active_recruit_notice_carver}} wins the dispute, but your name enters the report.
You stay out of it. {{npc_active_recruit_notice_carver}} packs the plates before the guard can seize them.
A guard accuses {{npc_active_recruit_notice_carver}} of forging a seal: the proof shows the emblem reversed. She insists the official matrix was copied from a print, not the other way around.
event.active_recruitment_new_cast_01_nam: You leave the tag with {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}}. He promises not to ring the bell without a body or certainty.
Leave the tag
You push too hard; the fishers shut their doors and the rumor grows.
Two accounts agree on the same quay. {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} closes the death ledger and moves.
Everyone saw a different boat and nobody will swear which one.
One fisher remembers a tug returning without its flag. {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} notes the detail.
Question the fishers
You follow an old mark and get the wrong ship announced as lost.
You also find a recent splice. {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} realizes the sailor is probably alive.
The fibers are too mixed to tie the rope to a specific quay.
You identify the rope as local tug line. {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} removes one name from the dead list.
Trace the rope
{{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} is preparing a wake for a sailor whose only remains are a brass tag and a length of rope. The family refuses the bell until a body comes home.
A Name Without a Body
You carry the tag to the named quay. {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} follows without ringing the bell.
Carry the tag
{{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} cuts a diagonal line across the tag: neither dead nor living, not yet.
Mark it unconfirmed
The family takes the tag back. {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} closes the ledger without entering the name.
Return the tag
On the back of the tag, {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} finally notices a fresh scratch that did not come from the sea. Someone handled it after the supposed wreck.
The Brass Tag
event.active_recruitment_new_cast_01_red: You slip between two carts; the crate reaches the post and your shoulder takes the hit.
You cut off the route and spot the real marked crate at the same time. {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} clearly owes you a favor.
The porter crosses the barrier before you. The red knot vanishes behind customs.
You stop the cart just before the barrier. {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} recovers the red cord without surrendering the crate.
Catch the porter
You read the wrong knot and accuse a dockhand who took nothing.
You also read the last knot: the quay clerk ordered the swap. {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} finally has a lead.
The marks are too quick to untangle before the crate leaves.
The pattern shows a crate swap, not a theft. {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} knows where to run.
Read the knots
You leave the quarrel to the quay. {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} remembers your face without asking for more.
Let the crate go
A porter is hauling the wrong crate toward customs. {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} runs after him, red cord knotted around one wrist, swearing the manifest was switched.
The Red Knot
You confirm the swap to the customs officer. {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} gets the crate back and adds a knot to the cord.
Back the story
The ledger reveals two different hands. {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} leaves with evidence instead of a fight.
Demand the manifest
You leave before the dispute becomes yours. {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} handles the rest alone.
Leave the post
The customs officer holds the crate and demands proof. {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} grips the knotted cord: every mark matches a delivery, but nobody here knows the system.
At the Customs Gate
event.active_recruitment_new_cast_01_thr: You front five hundred Berrys to break the deadlock. {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} knots the amount onto the wrist cord as a debt to you.
Pay one claim
You turn the crowd against you; one creditor demands five hundred Berrys immediately.
The crowd demands all three creditors’ ledgers. {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} is no longer the only one being questioned.
They stop shouting, but nobody withdraws a claim.
Two creditors agree to check their marks. {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} finally gets room to breathe.
Pressure the creditors
Your accounting charges the same debt twice; all three creditors turn on you.
You spot a deliberate duplicate across the three receipts. {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} turns the trap into evidence.
The accounts stay contradictory and the market bell rings before any agreement.
You reconstruct the order of exchanges. {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} can settle two debts and contest the third.
Untangle the claims
Three creditors surround {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} in the port market. Each shows a different receipt before closing bell; the knotted cord says only one account is still owed.
Three Debts, One Bell
The forged receipt turns to ash. {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} accepts losing the evidence to end the blackmail.
Burn the forgery
{{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} hands you half the forged receipt. The next knot on the cord marks your account, not a client’s.
Keep the torn receipt
You return the paper to the creditor. {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} says nothing, but unties one knot from the cord.
Return the receipt
The last receipt tears as {{npc_active_recruit_knot_runner}} compares it with the cord. One half bears the right seal; the other was copied to invent a debt that does not exist.
The Torn Receipt
event.active_recruitment_new_cast_01_wro: You lead the procession to the wrong door; the real family hears the death through rumor.
You also spot an open window and a figure answering to the dead man’s name. {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} nearly drops the bell.
The old street plans disagree and the procession waits in the rain.
You find the old address under a new number. {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} stops the bell at the right door.
Find the house
You let the procession move. {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} rings once, then stops when someone comes running from the street.
Let the bell ring
The crowd takes your doubt as an insult and rings the bell themselves.
The family demands the check with you. {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} can suspend the wake without losing their trust.
The procession slows, but nobody wants to abandon the ceremony.
You win a few minutes. {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} checks the ledger one last time.
Stop the procession
A procession follows {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} toward the home of a sailor declared dead. Halfway there, a child swears he saw the man alive this morning in the same blue coat.
The Wrong Dead Man’s Bell
The family discovers the survivor themselves. {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} folds away the bell without asking for thanks.
Let the family knock
The sailor is alive, gaunt and furious at the rumor. {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} strikes the name from the ledger before the whole family.
Open the door
You leave before the reveal. {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} stays to correct the ledger.
Leave before the door
Behind the door, someone coughs exactly as {{npc_active_recruit_wake_keeper}} raises the bell. The family freezes; the name carved on the tag is still hanging from the frame.
The Living Man’s Door

npc.active_recruit_notice_carver.name: Notice Carver
